title: Four AFL players to face no criminal charges after sexual assault allegations
content:
Four top Australian Rules Football players under investigation following allegations of sexual assault will face no criminal charges, police have confirmed.

Allegations of sexual assault were made against five Sydney Swans players in August, but Victoria Police confirmed in a statement on Friday that they would not be proceeding with criminal charges due to insufficient evidence.

Isaac Heeney, 30, Chad Warner, 25, Nick Blakey, 26, (who has since joined North Melbourne), Riley Bice, 26, and James Jordon, 25, had all been suspended by the Swans following an alleged incident at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne after their penultimate game of the regular season.

Bice was cleared as a suspect at the start of September, local media reported, but remained suspended from playing for the rest of the season. The Swans maintained the club-enforced sanctions were separate from the police investigation.

“Sexual Crimes Squad detectives received reports of sexual assault in East Melbourne on 17 August,” a Victoria Police statement read.

“The incident occurred at a hotel on Wellington Parade in the early hours of the morning.

“Following a thorough investigation and based on legal advice, Victoria Police will not proceed with criminal charges due to insufficient evidence.

“Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment.”

It was reported by ABC that three women are continuing to pursue civil action in relation to the allegations. John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers told the network his clients were “very disappointed and distressed” over the police investigation’s outcome. The players have denied any wrongdoing, as reported by BBC News. They released a joint-statement in August apologising for falling short of club standards and values.

The Swans made the decision to “torpedo” their finals season by suspending the players for the remainder of the campaign, in a mark of “how seriously” the club took the allegations, club chairman Andrew Pridham said in August.

The team finished second in the regular season before being beaten in the preliminary finals — one round before the Grand Final, AFL’s Super Bowl equivalent — by Fremantle.

The club said in a statement on Friday it stood by the decision to suspend the players.

“The Sydney Swans acknowledge today’s statement from Victoria Police that its investigation has concluded, with no charges laid against any Sydney Swans player,” the statement read.

“The club stood down players Riley Bice, Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney, James Jordan and Chad Warner in August 2026 because their conduct fell short of the standards of behaviour expected at the club.

“The club was clear from the outset that this decision was separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision.”

An AFL statement added: “The AFL endorsed the Sydney Swans standing down five players for the remainder of the season, including all finals matches, in response to behaviour that fell well short of the standards expected of those involved in Australian football.

“The five sanctioned players were also deemed by the AFL to be unavailable for selection for the AFL All Australian award.

“The AFL reserves the right to investigate if any further relevant information comes to light.”
